guardrails: Only activation-to-claim behavior may affect routing responsiveness.
READY-to-activation latency is system latency and never penalizes the worker.
UNKNOWN, stale, paused, offline, or merely unactivated presence never creates negative worker evidence.
Pending unexpired activations never count as failures.
Work-steal activations are measured separately and never train primary-routing responsiveness.
Claim-to-start and start-to-complete latency are descriptive only because task difficulty and execution complexity are confounded.
Automatic responsiveness adjustment is penalty-only, bounded, and remains zero until global and per-worker evidence thresholds are met.
This is capacity-response evidence, not a causal worker-quality ranking.
